definition: Google Flow, formerly known as Flow, is a generative AI video and multimedia creation tool developed by Google.
details: Introduced in 2025, Flow allows users to generate videos, music, and visual images using natural language prompts and uploaded media. It uses Veo, a text-to-video model, and Imagen, a text-to-image model, and is available through the Google Labs platform.

explainer.lead: Google Flow is a Google workspace for turning written prompts and reference images into AI-generated videos, images, and sound. It brings several generative-media models into one creative workflow, while Flow TV lets people browse clips and read the prompts behind them.

tiers.eli5: Imagine describing a tiny movie to a very quick artist who can draw it and make it move. You can also show Flow a picture to guide the result, and newer versions can add voices, background sounds, and music. Flow TV works like a gallery where you can watch what others made and see the instructions they used.
tiers.practitioner: Use Flow through Google Labs by writing natural-language prompts, optionally adding existing or generated reference images, and iterating at the scene or clip level. Veo handles video, Imagen and Nano Banana handle images, and Veo 3.1 adds synchronized dialogue, environmental effects, and music. Keep Flow Music separate in your mental model: it uses Lyria models to generate songs, playlists, and remixable compositions.
tiers.paperLevel: Google Flow is a generative-media application rather than a single model: F(p, r) maps a text prompt p and optional reference images r to video through Veo or images through Imagen and Nano Banana. Veo 3.1 extends video generation with synchronized dialogue, environmental effects, and music. The described workflow targets short scenes and clips, with audio capabilities added in later versions.

explainer.example: A user uploads a generated image of a lighthouse and prompts Flow to create a short scene of waves striking its base during a storm. Veo generates the video, and Veo 3.1 can add synchronized environmental sound, dialogue, or music; the finished clip and its prompt can then be explored through Flow TV.

usedIn.name: Google Labs
usedIn.detail: The platform through which users access Flow’s prompt-based media creation tools.

usedIn.name: Flow TV
usedIn.detail: Introduced in May 2025 for browsing AI-generated clips and reading the prompts used to create them.

usedIn.name: Google Flow Music
usedIn.detail: Uses Google’s Lyria models to generate songs, playlists, and remixable compositions from text prompts.

usedIn.name: Music production
usedIn.detail: Google’s 2026 partnerships with Believe and TuneCore expanded access to Flow Music for musicians and producers.

explainer.intuition: Flow acts as a shared creative workspace around several specialist generators. Instead of learning a separate tool for each medium, a user describes the desired result and supplies reference images when useful.
howItWorks: Write a natural-language description of the scene, image, or other media you want.
Optionally provide an existing or AI-generated reference image.
Flow uses Veo for video and Imagen or Nano Banana for images.
With Veo 3.1, video can include synchronized dialogue, environmental effects, and music.
Browse finished clips and their creation prompts on Flow TV.
explainer.whyItMatters: Flow combines capabilities previously spread across VideoFX, ImageFX, and Whisk, reducing the need to move between separate experimental tools. Google said users had generated more than 100 million videos through Flow by August 2025.
misconceptions: Flow is not one AI model; it is a tool built around models such as Veo and Imagen.
Flow TV is a platform for browsing clips and prompts, not the name of the video model.
Google Flow Music is a Lyria-based music platform associated with Flow, formerly known as ProducerAI.
